Apply Schema Validation, Stopping on Fatal Issues

Source: R/lib_data_loader.R
schval.Rd

Runs valsch() (or, for a list of rules, valrules()) and acts on the result: the first fatal issue stops with an error, and every warning-severity issue is raised as an R warning. Put it at the top of an analysis script so that a re-released file with a missing column stops the run before any result is computed.

Usage

schval(dfraw, prov)

Arguments

dfraw

The data frame to validate.

prov

A provenance list as returned by loadprov() (with a schema element), or one rule or a list of rules from rul(), run with valrules() under the same stop-on-fatal contract.

Value

Invisibly, TRUE if no issues were found and FALSE if only warning-severity issues were found (each raised as a warning). Errors if any fatal issue is present.

Details

Issues are handled in the order the validator returns them; a fatal issue stops at once, so warnings after it are not raised. With a list of rules the same contract applies to each rule's severity.

Unlike valsch(), this function refuses to check against nothing, because a validation that checks nothing must not report success. Errors: dfraw not a data frame; prov a data frame; prov NULL or an empty list; a list that mixes rules with other elements; an unnamed list that is not all rules; something other than a list; a provenance list with no schema element (the message names the elements it has, so a typo such as scheme shows); an empty schema (list(schema = list())).

Examples

prov <- list(schema = list(expected_columns = "id"))
schval(data.frame(id = 1), prov)
# A missing required column is fatal:
try(schval(data.frame(x = 1), prov))
#> Error : Missing required columns: id

# a warning-level issue is raised as a warning and the result is FALSE
ranged <- list(schema = list(numeric_ranges = list(v = c(min = 0, max = 1))))
ok <- withCallingHandlers(
  schval(data.frame(v = c(0.5, 3)), ranged),
  warning = function(w) {
    message("warning: ", conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
#> warning: Column 'v' has 1 value(s) outside [0, 1]
ok
#> [1] FALSE

# rules work the same way
rules <- list(rul("id_positive", function(v) v > 0, col = "id", sev = "fatal"))
try(schval(data.frame(id = c(1, -2)), rules))
#> Error : Rule 'id_positive' failed (1 of 2 rows)

# a provenance without a schema is refused, not passed
try(schval(data.frame(id = 1), list(scheme = list())))
#> Error : `prov` has no `schema` element (it has scheme): nothing would be validated
